question.text: A Cat II AIF structured as a COMPANY (not a trust) is taxed at the fund level on its business income. Under the ITA's Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) regime, what is the MAT rate and base applicable to this domestic corporate AIF (assuming it has NOT opted for Section 115BAA/BAB concessional regimes)?

answer.text: 30% of taxable income (MAT does not apply).
15% of BOOK PROFITS (plus surcharge and cess) if the MAT amount exceeds normal-provisions tax; MAT credit carries forward for 15 years.
18.5% of adjusted total income (that is AMT for non-corporates).

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: MAT is levied on domestic companies at 15% of BOOK PROFITS (plus applicable surcharge and cess) where the tax calculated under the MAT route exceeds the normal-provisions tax. MAT credit can be carried forward for 15 years. Companies that opt for Section 115BAA (22%) or 115BAB (15%) concessional regimes are NOT liable to MAT but also forfeit MAT credit going forward. The Trap: Option A ignores MAT altogether. Option C confuses MAT (corporates, 15% on book profits) with AMT (non-corporates, 18.5% on adjusted total income). Option D understates the MAT rate to 10%. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests both MAT (corporates) and AMT (non-corporates, 18.5%). Corporate taxation basics are also tested in XV and XXI-B at a lighter depth. Note: MAT does not apply to foreign companies satisfying treaty/PE conditions. Manager's Pro-Tip: Most Cat I/II AIFs are trusts precisely to avoid MAT's 15% book-profit floor. If a corporate structure is proposed (e.g., for a regulated insurance-pool LP), model MAT and AMT scenarios in the initial PPM tax chapter and quantify the drag vs a trust structure.
